key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than manage light: they also improve wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texturing is a practical design lever that can simultaneously boost efficiency, process quality, and device durability in perovskite photovoltaics and related optoelectronics.
method: Review of recently reported texture-related effects in perovskite-based devices
Focus on non-optical benefits: wetting, crystal quality, charge extraction, and stability
Synthesizes observations across solar cells, photodetectors, and LEDs
evidence_signal: The paper is a review of recent literature rather than a new experimental dataset, so its claims are based on reported device and materials improvements.
watch_item: Texture benefits may depend strongly on fabrication compatibility, surface chemistry, and whether added roughness introduces defects or process variability.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
